Alright, let me think this through. I'm sitting here at the start of the season, turning over in my head what I'll do this year with my 16.9 mu.

---

**My thinking as the farmer:**

I've been working this land for thirty years — I pretty much have a rhythm by now. The 16.9 mu isn't all one piece. About 6 mu is the western plot where the soil has always done better for cotton than for grain, so that's where my cotton stays. The other 10.9 mu I run wheat in winter, then maize right after — that's the main system around here, like most of my neighbors.

With just three of us in the household and some of us working off-farm, labor is the real pinch. That's honestly why I haven't expanded cotton — cotton picking eats up weeks. I already squeeze a lot of hired help from relatives during picking season.

**Wheat (10.9 mu) — already in the ground from last October:**
The wheat went in around October 10th last year, a variety I bought new — Jimai 22 type, what most people here plant. I paid about 40 yuan/mu for seed. Before planting I broadcast about 40 kg of 15-15-15 compound per mu and rotary-tilled it in. At jointing in March I'll topdress maybe 15 kg of urea per mu if the color looks right — if the crop's pale I'll push it closer to 20, if it's dark green I'll hold back. The extension guy a few years ago said 18 kg of N is enough, but I've always done a hair more on the topdress because I don't want to regret it come May. That puts my total N somewhere around 16-17 kg/mu.

Irrigation: I already gave it the winter water in December. I'll irrigate again at jointing (late March) and once more at flowering in early May if we haven't had decent rain by then. Three irrigations is usual. Well water costs me roughly 25 yuan/mu each time by the time I pay for the electricity and pump wear.

Weeds I spray once in spring with a broadleaf herbicide. Aphids sometimes need a shot late, we'll see. I'm hoping for around 420 kg/mu — that's what I usually get. Last year was 435, year before was closer to 400 because of the late frost.

**Maize (10.9 mu) — right after wheat harvest in June:**
Wheat comes off around June 10th, and I've got to get maize in the ground within a week. No time to plow — I no-till drill straight into the wheat stubble with a hired planter (pays about 30 yuan/mu including seed placement). Hybrid seed — I use Zhengdan 958 or whatever the seed shop has that looks similar, roughly 50 yuan/mu.

For fertilizer I use a one-shot approach — 40 kg of a slow-release compound (roughly 28-8-10 or similar) banded at planting, gives me about 11 kg N from the base. Then if the maize looks hungry around tasseling in late July, I'll side-dress 15 kg of urea per mu. Usually I end up doing it, so plan on it. That gets me to about 18 kg N total.

Irrigation for maize depends on the rains. Last two years I gave one irrigation at tasseling. If it's a dry July, two. I hope for 470 kg/mu — last year's was 485.

**Cotton (6 mu) — planting mid-to-late April:**
Cotton goes in around April 20th. I buy improved seed, about 60 yuan/mu — Bt cotton, because pink bollworm is still around and I don't want to spray that every week. Before planting I plow proper (unlike my maize ground) and work in about 40 kg of compound plus 10 kg of urea at planting. Then I topdress another 10 kg of urea at first squaring in late June and maybe 8 kg at boll-setting in July. So total N around 13-14 kg/mu — cotton doesn't take as much N as grain.

Cotton is where I spend real money on spray. Aphids early, spider mites in July, bollworm late. I'll spray 4-5 times over the season, maybe 15-20 yuan/mu per spray for product. Irrigation twice usually — once right after planting to get it up, once at peak flowering.

Labor is the killer on cotton. Multiple picks from mid-September through late October. Family does what we can, but I'll hire people for at least 20-25 days across the picking season. If lint price stays above 12 yuan/kg this year I'll come out okay. Price is the thing I can't control. I expect about 240 kg of lint per mu.

**What I'm worried about:**
Fertilizer prices are still high this year — compound is running 3.5-4 yuan/kg, urea around 2.8. That pinches. Honestly I've thought about cutting 2-3 kg of N off the wheat topdress to save money, but thirty years tells me skimping on topdress is how you lose 50 kg/mu of yield. Not worth it. Where I save is holding off on the extra maize irrigation unless the field is really showing stress.

Cash is the other thing. Off-farm work from my son helps, but I still need to front about 9,000 yuan in inputs before harvest. I plan to pay the planter and the big fertilizer bill on credit from the village shop and settle after wheat comes off.
